title: Paloma Business Reserve Rate Schedule by Returned Payouts
content:
Returned payouts decide the reserve rate on a withdrawal from a Paloma Business balance, the reserve rate being the percentage of the reserve basis kept back as the standing reserve. The payouts counted are those returned in the twelve months before the day of the withdrawal, counted from the day after the same calendar day twelve months earlier up to and including that day. A payout counts when it has a return record dated in that window.

| Payouts returned in the twelve-month window | Reserve rate |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 5 percent |
| Exactly one | 3 percent |
| None | 1 percent, the standing rate |

As a clause: two or more returned payouts set a reserve rate of 5 percent; exactly one sets 3 percent; none keeps the standing rate of 1 percent.

### Illustrations (hypothetical reserve basis of 40000.00 USD)

- Two payouts returned in the window: 5 percent, 2000.00 USD.
- One payout returned: 3 percent, 1200.00 USD.
- No payout returned: 1 percent, 400.00 USD.
- A payout returned thirteen months before the withdrawal is outside the window.
